jobs.description:
Overview

We are building a benchmark that tests how well AI agents handle real expert work in a terminal. We are hiring ML inference and serving experts to turn real, paid tasks from their jobs into expert-level Terminal-Bench challenges. Each task includes the environment, a working solution, and an automated check that proves the result is correct.

***THIS IS A TASK BASED COMPENSATION MODEL. PLEASE CHECK THE APPLICATION QUESTIONS FOR MORE DETAILS.***

Responsibilities

â¢ Design expert-level Terminal-Bench tasks that turn real, paid ML inference work from your own experience into challenges an AI agent must solve end to end.

â¢ Define the files, systems and environments each task runs on, such as model serving with streaming, so the challenge is realistic, reproducible and command-line solvable.

â¢ Write a working reference solution for every task and verify it runs end to end, sized for about 60 to 75 minutes of expert effort.

â¢ Build automated checks that objectively prove a result is correct, including cases where ML outputs go wrong silently, such as numerical drift or metric bugs.

â¢ Package tasks with Docker and Git so they are reproducible, and document the systems, tools, data and rules involved so reviewers can validate difficulty.

â¢ Iterate on tasks based on reviewer feedback and agent test runs, adjusting difficulty and fixing ambiguities so each task stays expert-level, fair and objectively gradable.

Skills/Experience

â¢ 3+ years doing ML inference or serving work hands-on (not only studying, selling or managing it), or a PhD plus active research in the subfield

â¢ Did this work in the last 3 years and can name the systems, tools, data and rules used

â¢ Trained, served or evaluated models at real scale (multi-GPU or production serving), not only notebooks or API calls

â¢ Hands-on with PyTorch or JAX internals and serving stacks such as vLLM, SGLang or TensorRT-LLM

â¢ Can explain how ML results go wrong without errors (numerical drift, metric bugs) and how to catch them

â¢ Technical fluency in Python and the command line, and with files, CSV/JSON, APIs or databases

â¢ Availability to start by early November 2026 and complete tasks of about 60 to 75 minutes each

Nice-to-have

â¢ AI lab or LLM infrastructure experience

â¢ Contributions to PyTorch, vLLM or SGLang

â¢ GPU profiling experience

â¢ Docker and Git proficiency

â¢ Experience writing automated tests

Process

â¢ Task vetting instead of an interview: complete a vetting task so the client can assess your task design

â¢ Paid per task; each task takes about 60 to 75 minutes

â¢ Work is delivered task by task, with reviewer feedback on submissions

â¢ Expected start in early November 2026
